title: Optional mathematics
blurb: Extra track: sets, matrices, limits, trig identities, and vectors — Nepal/CBSE optional style.

setlang.name: Set language
setlang.phrase: ∈ means “in the club.” ∪ is or, ∩ is and, ′ is not.
steps: Curly braces list elements: {1,2,3}.
x ∈ A means x is a member; x ∉ A means it is not.
Union ∪ = or; intersection ∩ = both; complement A′ = not in A (inside the universe).
setlang.exception: Order and repeats do not matter in a set: {1,2} = {2,1,1}. ∅ is empty — nothing is ∈ ∅. Do not confuse ⊂ (subset) with ∈ (element).

setcount.name: Counting with sets
setcount.phrase: n(A∪B) = n(A)+n(B)−n(A∩B). Subtract the double-counted overlap.
steps: Add the sizes of A and B.
Subtract n(A∩B) once (it was counted twice).
For three sets, use the full inclusion–exclusion formula.
setcount.exception: If A and B are disjoint, n(A∩B)=0 and you just add. n(A) counts elements, not a probability — divide by n(U) only when asked for a probability.

matintro.name: Matrix shape & add
matintro.phrase: Rows by columns: m×n. Add entrywise — same shape only.
steps: Read size as rows × columns.
Addition: add matching positions; sizes must match.
Scalar multiply: multiply every entry by the number.
matintro.exception: You cannot add a 2×3 to a 3×2. Matrix multiplication is not entrywise addition — that comes later.

matdet.name: Determinant & inverse idea
matdet.phrase: det = ad − bc. Inverse exists only if det ≠ 0.
steps: For [[a,b],[c,d]], compute ad − bc.
If det ≠ 0, A⁻¹ = (1/det) [[d,−b],[−c,a]].
Check: A A⁻¹ = I.
matdet.exception: det = 0 means singular — no inverse. Do not swap the sign pattern on the off-diagonal by mistake.

limintro.name: Limits intro
limintro.phrase: A limit asks: what do the outputs approach as x approaches a?
steps: Try plugging x = a into f(x).
If you get a normal number, that is usually the limit (for continuous pieces).
If you get 0/0, factor or simplify, then plug in again.
limintro.exception: A hole or jump can make the limit differ from f(a), or make left/right limits disagree. “Approaches” is not the same as “equals” at a.

trigid.name: Trig identity extras
trigid.phrase: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1. Divide by cos² → 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ.
steps: Start from sin² + cos² = 1 on the unit circle.
Divide by cos²θ: tan² + 1 = sec².
Divide by sin²θ: 1 + cot² = cosec².
trigid.exception: These assume cos θ ≠ 0 when you create tan/sec forms (and sin ≠ 0 for cot/cosec). Identities hold where the functions are defined.

trigcomp.name: Cofunction & signs
trigcomp.phrase: sin(90°−θ)=cos θ. ASTC: All Sugar Tea Coffee for signs.
steps: Complement: sin↔cos, tan↔cot, sec↔cosec with 90°−θ.
For angles past 90°, reduce to a reference angle.
ASTC tells which functions are positive in each quadrant.
trigcomp.exception: Cofunction identities need the complement (90°−θ), not 180°−θ (that keeps the name for sine). Know your calculator mode.

vecintro.name: Vectors intro
vecintro.phrase: A vector has size and direction. ⟨a,b⟩ adds componentwise; length √(a²+b²).
steps: Write a plane vector as ⟨a,b⟩ or ai + bj.
Add/subtract matching components; multiply by a scalar on each.
Magnitude |⟨a,b⟩| = √(a²+b²).
vecintro.exception: Position vs free vector: the same ⟨a,b⟩ can start anywhere. |a+b| is not usually |a|+|b|. A scalar has no direction.

vecdot.name: Dot product intro
vecdot.phrase: a·b = a₁b₁ + a₂b₂. Zero dot means perpendicular.
steps: Multiply matching components and add.
Also a·b = |a||b| cos θ.
If a·b = 0 (and neither is zero), the vectors are perpendicular.
vecdot.exception: Dot product is a number, not a vector. Parallel vectors have cos θ = ±1, not necessarily a zero dot.

setops.name: Subset & power set
setops.phrase: A ⊆ B if every element of A sits in B. Power set: all subsets — 2ⁿ of them.
steps: Check subset: each member of A must be in B.
Proper subset ⊂ usually means ⊆ but not equal.
A finite set with n elements has 2ⁿ subsets (including ∅ and itself).
setops.exception: ∈ is for elements; ⊆ is for sets. {1} ∈ {{1}} is true, but 1 ∈ {{1}} is false. ∅ is a subset of every set.
